verdict.why: Resetting last_try on a reset is intentional to start backoff anew
Later change adds mapping for 'rm' to 'delete', confirming the original direct use was a bug.
busy already includes selecting, so the check is present
The code returns true for any uninitialized payload, marking it complete incorrectly.
The original jq command passes the token via --arg, exposing it in the process command line.
The original return uses d.model directly without length restriction, matching the finding.
The original command places String(id) before --json, causing the flag to be ignored as described
The unqualified import indeed shadows Qt's Color type, and the later alias import fixes it.
The later change replaces the manifest.__sourceDir access, confirming the original code was faulty.
The Process element does not have a suppressProcessOutput property, so the assignment on line 722 is invalid and will cause a runtime error.
The script uses --property/--type disable instead of the intended --missing-property/--missing-type flags, suppressing all warnings.
The later change adds implicit size to prevent the slot collapse, confirming the missing size was a real defect.
The import directly requires a running Quickshell process, causing failures in headless contexts.
The line directly returns the internal batchList as JSON, confirming the described exposure.
The rfind approach can match braces inside strings/comments, leading to incorrect insertion point.
The original onPressed directly called root.toggle/refresh instead of using triggerPress, confirming the described defect.
The original code sets command without setting previewProc.kind, which was later fixed by adding previewProc.kind = "file"
The line calls a function, not a read‑only property, so no TypeError occurs.
The original line captured unbounded JSON output, enabling memory exhaustion, which was later mitigated by limiting the size
The original cp command copies the whole omarchy directory, which the later change corrects by copying only needed files.
The original code deletes the signal file, matching the finding's issue.
The code resets alert and sent flags on !onBattery, matching the described defect.
The binding is standard and does not create a circular dependency
The original code only falls back to title‑based lookup, which can fail when the title doesn't match the desktop file name.
The original line checks only installNote, missing install availability, leading to misleading UI.
The except clause omits TypeError, allowing it to escape and crash the program.
The code uses manifest.__sourceDir which can be stripped, resulting in an empty pluginDir
The later change adds extra guards, confirming the original condition was faulty.
The HOOK_PATH variable includes a hard‑coded .py extension, which can cause the hook to fail when the script is named without that extension.
The die statement builds the message without a reason when $why is empty, matching the finding.
The code sets explicit bottomLeftRadius and bottomRightRadius, which the later change replaces the Rectangle with an Item, confirming the issue.
The command uses a literal '~' which is not expanded, causing deletion to fail
The original line passes the whole command as one string, which later was corrected to use an argument array, confirming the described defect.
The radius() call is made without validating its return before using it in canvas operations
The function builds a path '/everything/{object_id}' instead of the required hash fragment
The original test uses only -e and -d, missing -L, so dangling symlinks are not detected.
The original line adds svcName unconditionally, so an undefined value becomes a literal "undefined" argument causing backend errors
The original `visible` expression references child `.visible` properties, causing a feedback loop that can lock the row invisible.
The capture call is invoked without examining its return value, so failures are ignored.
The original loop only checks activeItem equality, missing the foreign marker case, which the later change fixes.
